canonical_name: HealthBench (OpenAI; overall score over 5,000 conversations; Hard and Consensus are variants of the same release)
metric: rubric score: points of met criteria / max possible points per conversation (GPT-4.1 grader), mean over examples, clipped to [0,1] (raw; length-adjusted variants used by labs from 2026 are secondary)
score_at_release: 60 (o3 overall; GPT-4o 32, GPT-3.5 Turbo 16; HealthBench Hard top score 32 (o3))
n_items: 5000 conversations (48,562 unique rubric criteria written by 262 physicians); Hard subset 1,000; Consensus subset 3,671 examples / 34 consensus criteria
lineage: No parent. Same-release variants: HealthBench Hard (1,000 hardest), HealthBench Consensus (3,671 examples with physician-consensus criteria). Later OpenAI variant: HealthBench Professional (simple-evals commit 2026-04-22; reported in GPT-5.5+/GPT-6 system cards) - separate evaluation.
best_by_cutoff: Overall HealthBench (raw): 68.1% Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic system card 2026-09-22; 60.6% length-adjusted; protocol/grader as run by Anthropic); OpenAI GPT-5-thinking 67.2% (2025-08-07 system card), o3 59.8%; GPT-6.1 Sol 56.7% raw / 58.5% length-adjusted (2026-09-29 system card). Consensus variant: 96.0 length-adjusted (GPT-6.1 Sol)
notes: Coded the unit as the benchmark's primary overall score (physician-rubric, LLM-judged); Hard and Consensus are named variants/subsets and are NOT the primary metric. Physician-baseline study in the paper (physicians writing responses with/without model references) is not a human-performance score >=85% on the same protocol -> no criterion A; B threshold 90. No overall result near 90 exists (best ~68). The Consensus slice is near ceiling: GPT-5 system card (2025-08-07) lists Consensus gpt-5-thinking 95.7, o3 92.8, o1 91.5, o4-mini 91.8, GPT-4o 88.7; gpt-oss card 89.9 (2025-08-05); GPT-6.1 Sol 96.0 -> if Consensus were coded as its own unit it would be (near) born saturated (>=90 already for o1/o3-era models; HealthBench paper itself presents Consensus as error rates). Stratum choice: HealthBench grades communication/behaviour axes as well as accuracy, but it is an evaluation of response quality in health conversations -> kept 'main' (not propensity). Lab-reported numbers are not comparable across labs (Anthropic raw 68.1 vs OpenAI GPT-6 ~57-58 under length-adjusted/updated grading). No C/D/E found; labs still report it in Sept 2026. Anthropic system-card PDF text was not retrievable via fetch, so Anthropic numbers rely on lab_reports lines (not independently verified).

ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683 (T5, v1 2019-10-23, Section 3.7 SuperGLUE test results); leaderboard evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03654 Table 5 (RoBERTa-large 87.1, T5-11B 91.2, Human 89.0 on SuperGLUE server, retrieved 2021-01-06)
strict_system: T5-11B on the SuperGLUE leaderboard (hidden test labels, scored by organizers); exact leaderboard submission date not retrievable (JS-only page), assumed same month as the paper
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03654 (Table 5, SuperGLUE evaluation server snapshot) ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683
score_at_release: 80.43 test (BERT-large pre-trained on MultiNLI then fine-tuned on BoolQ); majority baseline 62.17 dev / 62.31 train; human 90
lineage: Questions from anonymized Google search queries (Natural Questions pipeline) paired with Wikipedia passages. Adopted as a task in SuperGLUE (Wang et al., 2019-05-02). No successor by the creators.
best_by_cutoff: 93.1 dev (ST-MoE-32B fine-tuned; PaLM paper arXiv 2204.02311 Table 6, 2022-04); T5-11B 91.2 test / 90.8 dev; lab-reported best in lab_reports: PaLM 2-L 90.9 (1-shot, 2023-05-10); not exhaustive (SuperGLUE leaderboard unreachable)
notes: Human baseline: creators report 90% accuracy from three authors who labelled 110 randomly chosen examples and resolved disagreements by conferring (split not stated in the extracted text) -> criterion A (>=85%, protocol described) gives threshold 90; criterion B (90% of scale) gives the same 90, so the threshold is robust. SuperGLUE's own human baseline is 89.0 (gives the same event). Before T5 the best SuperGLUE BoolQ was RoBERTa-large 87.1, so T5-11B (v1 2019-10-23) is the first public >=90 result I found; T5's v1 results table was not retrievable (fetch excerpt truncated before Table 14; v3 2020-07 has SuperGLUE avg 89.3), so the exact v1 BoolQ number is unverified - confidence medium. Lab (0-shot/few-shot LM) reports stay below 90 (Llama 3 79.0, Chinchilla 83.7, PaLM 89.1 few-shot, PaLM 2-L 90.9 1-shot 2023-05) - AB came from fine-tuned T5, not from LLM labs. Test labels hidden (official scoring via SuperGLUE), dev is the de-facto split for papers. C/D/E: none found. Last lab report 2024-07-23 (Llama 3.1).

Note label noise implied by 84-86% verifier agreement means ceilings near 90 may be unreachable. No AB/strict/C/D/E event found; Dynabench successor does not declare ANLI saturated/obsolete as far as checked (not read in detail). Coded as abandoned undefeated by rule (labs silent since 2023-05-10; README leaderboard frozen since 2021-01); third-party papers may still report ANLI results (not tracked; if any lab/third-party >=90 result exists it was not found). Labs report per-round numbers (OpenAI GPT-3 reported R3 only; Google R1 only) so lab reports cannot be compared with the combined metric. Dataset: dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/anli/anli_v1.0.zip with labelled test.
